newsitem.title: FRANCE: Little impact seen in French civil service strike.
newsitem.headline: Little impact seen in French civil service strike.

text.p: French civil servants planned to stage a 24-hour strike over wage demands Thursday but the impact of their protest will be blunted because public transportation is not involved.
Seven unions called on the country's four million public employees to stop work, saying the government wage offer for this year and next will cut their purchasing power.
The stoppage comes against a background of social unrest as the government enforces budget austerity to comply with criteria to join the European single currency in 1999.
Demonstrations and rallies were expected to jam traffic in cities and many schools will be closed, but the protest is not expected to cause major disruptions to the public.
Public transport workers, who are holding separate wage talks, said they will not join the protest.
Thursday's strike should mostly affect schools, hospitals and postal services.
Automation of services at national telephone and utility companies means the stoppage will have little consequences on most consumers.
The unions called the strike after turning down a government offer of a 2.8 percent pay rise for 1997 and 1998, which they said will not compensate for a 1996 pay freeze.
